editorial.headline: Glass, Doors and Frames: An Open Route for Foreign Investment in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This construction-finishing activity spans glazing, curtain walls, doors, frames and windows—and is open to PMA nationally and in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity sits in the finishing stage of buildings and civil works: the work of fitting glass into walls, windows, doors and other openings in residential, non-residential and civil construction. Its scope also reaches glass-and-aluminium curtain walls, changes to glass colour and glass coatings, and the installation of doors, frames, windows, and door or window frames made from wood or other materials. Automatic and revolving doors sit outside the stated door-installation scope. In practical terms, this is the trade that brings the enclosure and openings of a building into their finished form.

The code is available across the full business-scale range recorded: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the activity is not framed as the preserve of a single operating scale. It can describe work undertaken by a micro enterprise as readily as a large business, provided the actual work remains within the defined installation scope. The focus is specific: installing and finishing glazing, doors, frames and windows, rather than treating every construction task around a building as part of the same activity.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clear. The activity is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. A PMA company may therefore be wholly foreign-owned under the national position recorded here. Bali does not reverse that result. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island, permanently, but this activity is recorded as not blocked. The stated reason is that, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High or High—so it does not fall within the moratorium’s blocked risk bands.

The honest Bali reading is consequently straightforward: PMA registration for this activity is open in Bali. That is not a softened version of a national permission facing a provincial prohibition; the Bali record expressly says it is not blocked by the moratorium. The national 100% ceiling remains the foreign-ownership figure, while the Bali result turns on the recorded risk treatment and the moratorium’s defined reach. For founders, the essential discipline is to keep the business description anchored to the actual installation work: glass, curtain walls, coatings, doors, frames and windows, as the scope sets out.
